questions: Does cycle_count_escalator.check_session_total honour the escalation-suppression marker as its docstring claims?
If not, what timestamp does the suppression comparison need, and does the data to produce it already exist?
What is the blast radius of changing stall_walk's session-total counter, and which existing tests pin its shape?

findings.statement: check_session_total never reads the suppression marker: it calls _suppression_active(session_id, None) and that helper returns False unconditionally when first_match_ts is None, so the marker file is never opened
The docstring asserts the opposite of the behaviour: 'Respects the same suppression marker as check.' No test covers suppression in session-total mode, which is why the drift survived since Phase 69
findings.evidence: qor/scripts/cycle_count_escalator.py:68; the only suppression test is tests/test_cycle_count_escalator.py:108, which exercises the consecutive-streak check only

findings.statement: Both modes are surfaced together at /qor-audit Step 0.5 and /qor-plan Step 2c and the documented decline path writes the marker, so a declined session-total escalation re-fires on every subsequent audit in the session and each decline appends another severity-2 orchestration_override event

The timestamp the comparison needs already exists in the records the counter reads; stall_walk.count_session_signature_totals walks every VETO record and discards each record's ts, keeping only the per-signature count

count_session_signature_totals has exactly one production consumer and its return shape is pinned by six test assertions, so the fix must add a sibling accessor rather than widen the existing return type
findings.evidence: qor/scripts/cycle_count_escalator.py:71 is the sole non-test caller; tests/test_session_total_signature_count.py:70,80,99,116,150 and tests/test_findings_signature_schema_parity.py:101

findings.statement: The consecutive mode compares the marker against the OLDEST audit in the current run, so the session-total mode must compare against the oldest record contributing to the over-threshold signature for the two modes to mean the same thing by the same words
findings.evidence: qor/scripts/stall_walk.py:70-72 assigns first_match_ts on every accepted record while walking newest-to-oldest, leaving the oldest
